### The Father of Canaan
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/father-canaan
Passage: Genesis 9:22
Points:
- Righteous Noah's fall demonstrates that even faithful believers can stumble into sin after enduring great trials.
- Wine is a gift from God, but abusing it through overindulgence reflects a heart that loves the gift more than the Giver.
- Noah acted carelessly by uncovering himself, leaving himself vulnerable to exposure and shame.
- Ham dishonored his father by looking on his nakedness and gossiping to his brothers rather than covering him.
- Christians must remain vigilant, guarding against carelessness after seasons of faithfulness.

### 3 Lessons We Can Learn from Noah’s Drunkenness
Author: Melinda Eye Cooper
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/faith/bible-study/lessons-we-can-learn-from-noahs-drunkenness.html
Passage: Genesis 9:20-23
Points:
- Scripture does not forbid alcohol entirely, but drinking to the point of drunkenness is a sin.
- Intoxication destroys self-control and lowers a person's defenses, leading to bad decisions and shameful situations.
- Ham dishonored his father by exposing his vulnerability, whereas Shem and Japheth acted respectfully by covering him.
- Noah’s lapse in judgment and Ham’s dishonor triggered long-lasting generational consequences for their family.
- Believers are urged to rely on the Holy Spirit to cultivate self-control and glorify God in all their actions.
